title: Big, small, long, short, heavy, light

parent.learn: Size words come in pairs: big–small, long–short, tall–short, heavy–light.
parent.why: Each word only makes sense when comparing two things. A dog is big next to a mouse but small next to an elephant.

parent.learn: To see which is longer, line the ends up.
parent.why: If one pencil starts further back, it can look shorter than it is. Starting both at the same line makes the comparison fair.

parent.learn: Heavy and light are felt, not seen.
parent.why: A big balloon is light and a small stone is heavy, so size alone does not tell weight — hold one in each hand to check.

parent.learn: Measure with hand-spans, steps or paper clips.
parent.why: Counting how many spans long something is turns “long” into a number. Different hands give different numbers — that is why we later use a ruler.

ask: Which is longer: your shoe or Papa's shoe? Put them side by side.
Who is taller: you or the door handle?
Hold a book and a pencil. Which is heavier?
How many hand-spans long is the table?
How many of your steps from the door to your bed?
Find something in the room that is longer than your arm.
Which holds more water: a bucket or a cup?

rounds.h: An elephant is much bigger than a mouse.
A cherry is tiny next to a watermelon.
A giraffe's long neck makes it taller than a dog.
An elephant is heavy; a feather is so light it floats.
A snake is much longer than a caterpillar.
A balloon is full of air and floats — very light. A brick is heavy.
A pencil fits in your hand; a door is taller than you.
A bucket is much bigger inside, so it holds more.
Books add weight. The empty bag is the same bag with nothing in it.
A tall building has many floors — taller than a house, tree or cat.

rounds.t: A table is 6 hand-spans long. A bed is 10 hand-spans long. Which is longer?
rounds.h: 10 spans is more than 6 spans, so the bed is longer.

rounds.t: Rani's pencil is 5 clips long. Sam's pencil is 7 clips long. Whose is shorter?
rounds.h: 5 clips is fewer than 7 clips, so Rani's pencil is shorter.

rounds.t: A big man walks across the room in 8 steps. Will a small child need more steps or fewer?
rounds.h: A child's steps are smaller, so it takes more of them to cover the same room.

rounds.t: A big balloon and a small stone. Which is heavier?
rounds.h: Size does not tell weight. The balloon is mostly air; the stone is solid.
9 is the biggest number of clips, so that ribbon is the longest.
